Import a callsign certificate backup (.p12) exported from TrustedQSL, including its private key. A .tq6 file alone is not enough. Signing stays on this phone. The backup is encrypted locally and excluded from cloud backup. Certificate passwords are not saved.

Confirm the actual operating location for these contacts, not today’s GPS position. The grid is required; other fields are optional TQSL codes. Example for China: GD, CQ 24, ITU 44. Upload separate batches for different locations.

This submits the signed snapshot shown below to ARRL LoTW. Check the callsign, location and contacts before continuing. Acceptance does not mean a QSL confirmation.
Submit %1$d QSOs
LoTW accepted the file containing %1$d QSOs for processing. This is not a QSL confirmation. Check LoTW activity, then download QSOs after processing.
LoTW rejected the file. Check the callsign certificate and LoTW activity. No contacts were marked received.
Submission result is unknown; LoTW may have received the file. Check LoTW activity and download QSOs before retrying. This batch will not be resent automatically.
This preview expired or was already used. Sign and preview again.
Cannot unlock this .p12 file. Check the certificate backup password (not the LoTW login password), or export the certificate again from TQSL.
The callsign certificate is expired or not yet valid. Check the phone date and import a valid certificate.
A valid LoTW callsign certificate with one matching RSA private key is required. .tq6 and key-only requests cannot sign logs.
Cannot complete this local operation. Check device storage and certificate access. No automatic upload retry was attempted.
A contact’s station callsign does not match the certificate. Correct the log or filter for the matching callsign.
A contact is in the future or outside the certificate’s permitted QSO date range.
Enter a valid 4, 6 or 8 character operating grid.
Invalid TQSL region/county code for this DXCC entity. Check the code and its parent region, or leave optional fields blank.
CQ zone must be 1–40; ITU zone must be 1–90.
Enter an IOTA code such as AS-001, or leave it blank.
A contact’s mode is not recognized by the bundled ARRL configuration.
A contact needs a valid band; any TX/RX frequency must agree with its band.
Use an official LoTW satellite name and a QSO date within that satellite’s operating period.
A contact has an invalid callsign or is incomplete.
A contact’s recorded operating grid differs from this station location. Filter a matching batch or correct the location.
Limit each upload batch to 10,000 contacts using logbook filters.
